summary: This resolution lets the House automatically concur in the Senate amendment to H.R. 7147 (further FY2026 consolidated appropriations) by substituting the text of Rules Committee Print 119-21.

scores.thoughts: The resolution directly facilitates passage of H.R. 7147, a consolidated appropriations measure for FY 2026. By providing for House concurrence in the Senate amendment, the bill authorizes and enacts federal spending, which aligns with expanding government spending.
The bill text contains no provisions related to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue policy.
No specific healthcare policy changes or coverage mandates are addressed; any funding implications are incidental to general appropriations and not the focus.
The legislation does not address firearms regulations, rights, or enforcement.
No immigration pathways, border enforcement, or related legal changes are mentioned.
The bill contains no language concerning abortion access or restrictions.
While appropriations bills can fund defense, this procedural resolution does not specify or alter defense spending levels or policy.
No environmental regulations, protections, or funding directives are present.
The text does not modify welfare programs, eligibility, or benefit levels.
No education funding formulas, school choice provisions, or federal involvement changes are included.
The bill does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related criminal penalties.
No sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation reforms are addressed.
The legislation contains no trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization measures.
While appropriations affect deficits, the bill itself does not prioritize debt reduction or explicitly accept deficit spending as policy.
No legal protections or limitations concerning LGBTQ+ individuals are addressed.
The bill does not modify foreign assistance levels or programs.
No voting access, election integrity, or reform provisions are present.
The legislation does not regulate technology, data privacy, or oversight mechanisms.
No worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility measures are included.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or civil rights priorities.
